signature: SEBASTIAN [master’s mark: cartouche with cock with tail spread, initials “S H”] HAINLEIN / 16. NVRM [master’s mark (extends through both lines of signature)] BERG. 42.
dimensions: bo 10.2, be 105, le 2615, h 1075, bell sec. entry 1
literature: Wörthmüller 1955: 445; Langwill 1974: 69; Van der Meer 1979: 92, Abb. 147-48 (photos); Van der Meer 1982: 34; Van der Meer 1983: 142 (photo); Fischer 1984: 43; 300 Jahre 1985: 289 (photo); Huber 1989: 355.
remarks: Flat slide-stays, engraved with blossoms and tendrils and each with two dragon-head clasps. Some ferrules have simple ring pattern; some also have cast borders with leaf pattern; others have dragon-scale pattern in middle; others have a wreath with a small half-sphere; still others have a border with pointed teeth and round arches. One flat bell-stay engraved with angel playing a trombone; eyelet off-center to bell-pipe side; sleeve adjacent to bell-stay has engraved blossom on both sides; hinge plate adjacent to bell stay in leaf form with engraved leaf pattern. Ring in bell bow, mounted on leaf-shaped saddle engraved with zigzag pattern. Bell only slightly flared. Garland has cast rim wire with leaf design; engraved tooth pattern on inner border; bell has engraving of the three Nuremberg coats of arms with an undulating cord and two tassels. Van der Meer 1979b says Hainlein played trombone, and at peace banquet given by Swedish field marshal Karl Gustav in Nuremberg, he played a Quart-bass trombone in F. From him a trombone was ordered for the Nuremberg Pfeifergericht, the granting in Frankfurt of freedom from customs duties for the Nuremberg Stadtpfeifer. Hainlein also made a bass trombone for the Salzburg archbishop Lodron.
